mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and increased production costs, negatively impacting corporate profit margins and thus S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE decreases > 0.5% in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real estate sales (HOUST) signals growing consumer confidence and demand, which typically leads to increased economic activity and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of instances following an increase in HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a weakening supply side of the economy, which can lead to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO decreases > 1% in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% MoM, it signals a potential inflationary environment with accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate continued low rates.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase > 200k in a month, it signals a strong labor market and potential wage inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies face higher costs.
regime_hint: tight labor market with strong job growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200k.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) signals growing consumer demand, which typically leads to increased economic activity and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances where RSAFS increases > 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative and industrial production (INDPRO) decreases > 1% in 3 months, it signals a recessionary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth < 0% and INDPRO decreases > 1% in 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 growth < 0% and INDPRO decreases > 1% in 3 months.
